components.name: Button
components.summary: Triggers an action: save, submit, open, delete.
components.overview: Button is the primary way people act on a page. It is a native <button> with four variants (primary, secondary, ghost and destructive), three sizes, optional leading and trailing icons and a loading state that keeps its width while it works.
whenToUse: To submit a form, confirm a dialog or start a task.
To open an overlay (a dialog, a menu, a drawer) from a clear label.
For the one most important action in a view, use the primary variant.
whenNotToUse: To go to another page: use Link, so it behaves like a link (middle-click, open in new tab).
For an on/off state such as Bold or Show archived: use Toggle.
For an icon with no visible text: use IconButton, which requires an accessible name.
do: Start labels with a verb and say what happens: "Save changes", "Invite member".
Keep one primary button per view or dialog; make the rest secondary or ghost.
Use the destructive variant for destructive actions, and confirm them with an AlertDialog.
Use loading while an async action runs, so people don't click twice.
dont: Don't disable a submit button to signal a validation problem; let people submit and show the errors.
Don't use vague labels such as "OK", "Yes" or "Click here".
Don't put two primary buttons side by side.
accessibility: Renders a native <button> (type="button" unless you set one), so Enter and Space activate it.
loading sets aria-busy and aria-disabled and ignores clicks, but keeps the button focusable.
Icons are decorative; the label is the accessible name.
components.ai: Using pada-ds (React) or pada-ds-angular, add a "Save changes" primary Button and a secondary "Cancel" Button to the form footer. Show the primary button's loading state while the save request is pending. Use Pada tokens only; no custom colours.

components.name: ButtonGroup
components.summary: A labelled row or column of related buttons that share a size and variant.
components.overview: ButtonGroup puts related buttons together as a role="group" named by label. Buttons without their own size or variant take the group's, and attached joins them into one segmented shape. Every button keeps its own tab stop.
whenToUse: For a small set of related actions: Previous / Next, Zoom in / Zoom out, Export / Print.
When the actions should read as one unit visually.
whenNotToUse: For a single choice between options with a pressed state: use ToggleGroup or SegmentControl.
For a full bar of controls with one tab stop and arrow keys: use Toolbar.
For a main action with alternatives in a menu: use SplitButton.
do: Always give the group a label that describes the set ("Text alignment", "Pagination").
Keep the group short: two to four buttons.
Set size and variant on the group so every button matches.
dont: Don't mix primary and secondary buttons in an attached group.
Don't use a group to fake tabs or a radio choice.
accessibility: role="group" with the label as its accessible name.
Each button stays a separate tab stop: a group of actions is not a toolbar.
components.ai: With Pada, render a ButtonGroup labelled "Text alignment" with attached secondary small buttons Left, Center and Right, each with a leading icon (align_left, align_center, align_right).

components.name: IconButton
components.summary: A square button that shows only an icon and is named by a label.
components.overview: IconButton is a compact square button for familiar actions such as close, more, edit or delete. It defaults to the ghost variant and requires an accessible name, because there is no visible text.
whenToUse: In dense UI: table rows, toolbars, card headers, dialog corners.
For actions whose icon is universally understood (close, search, more).
whenNotToUse: When the action is the main call to action: use Button with a label.
When the icon's meaning is not obvious: add a visible label instead of relying on a tooltip.
do: Always pass a label (aria-label) that names the action: "Close", "Delete row".
Set tooltip to show the label on hover and focus for sighted users.
Use the same size as neighbouring controls.
dont: Don't use an IconButton for a destructive action without confirmation.
Don't put several unlabelled IconButtons in a row with similar icons.
accessibility: Native <button>; the label is its accessible name and the icon is hidden from assistive technology.
Has a minimum hit area that follows density tokens.
components.ai: With Pada, add an IconButton with the "more_horizontal" icon and label "Row actions" to each table row. It opens a DropdownMenu with Edit and Delete. Turn on the IconButton's tooltip so the label also shows on hover and focus.

components.name: Link
components.summary: A text link to another page or resource.
components.overview: Link is a styled native <a> for navigation. It supports an accent or neutral tone, underline on hover or always, and an external mode that opens in a new tab and says so. In React, asChild puts the Pada styles on your router's link.
whenToUse: To navigate to another page, section or site.
Inline in body text, help text and empty states.
whenNotToUse: To perform an action that changes data: use Button.
For the main call to action of a page: use a Button (it can render as a link with asChild).
do: Write link text that makes sense out of context: "Read the billing guide", not "Click here".
Use external for links that leave your app, so people know a new tab will open.
In React, wrap router links with asChild; in Angular, put dsLink on the <a routerLink>.
dont: Don't use a link with an onClick and no href.
Don't remove the underline from links inside paragraphs; colour alone isn't enough.
accessibility: Native <a href>, so it works with the keyboard, context menus and middle-click.
External links add visually hidden text ("opens in a new tab").
components.ai: With Pada, render an inline Link "Read the billing guide" in the help text under the plan selector, pointing to /docs/billing. Use my router's link component through asChild (React) or put dsLink on the routerLink anchor (Angular).

components.name: SplitButton
components.summary: A main action joined to a chevron that opens related actions.
components.overview: SplitButton joins a primary action ("Save") to a chevron button that opens related alternatives ("Save as draft", "Save and publish"). SplitButton.Root sets the variant and size for both halves; the chevron (SplitButton.Splitter) is usually a DropdownMenu trigger.
whenToUse: When one action is the common default and a few variants are occasionally needed.
In toolbars and form footers where space is tight.
whenNotToUse: When the options are equally likely: use a DropdownMenu with a labelled trigger.
When there is only one action: use Button.
do: Make the main half do the most common action, with a clear verb.
Name the splitter with label ("More save options").
Keep the menu short and closely related to the main action.
dont: Don't put unrelated or destructive actions in the menu.
Don't use the deprecated Button split prop; use SplitButton.
accessibility: Two native buttons, each a tab stop. The splitter announces its label and aria-expanded.
The menu follows the WAI-ARIA Menu Button pattern (arrows, Home/End, type-ahead, Escape).
components.ai: With Pada, build a SplitButton whose main action is "Save" and whose chevron (label "More save options") opens a DropdownMenu with "Save as draft" and "Save and publish".

components.name: Toggle
components.summary: A button that stays pressed, for an on/off option.
components.overview: Toggle is a two-state button: Bold, Italic, Show archived, Mute. It is announced with aria-pressed and can be controlled (pressed) or uncontrolled (defaultPressed).
whenToUse: For formatting and view options inside editors and toolbars.
When the option takes effect immediately and is visible in the UI.
whenNotToUse: For settings that save a preference: use Switch.
For picking one of several options: use ToggleGroup or SegmentControl.
do: Keep the label constant; the pressed state shows whether it's on.
Give icon-only toggles an aria-label and a Tooltip.
dont: Don't change the label between states ("Mute" / "Unmute"); screen readers already say pressed.
Don't use a Toggle to submit or navigate.
accessibility: Native <button> with aria-pressed="true|false"; Enter and Space switch it.
State is exposed as data-state="on|off" for styling.
components.ai: With Pada, add Bold, Italic and Underline Toggles (icon-only, each with an aria-label and a Tooltip) to the editor toolbar, bound to the editor's formatting state.

components.name: ToggleGroup
components.summary: A segmented set of toggles with one tab stop and arrow-key navigation.
components.overview: ToggleGroup groups related toggles. With type="single" one item can be pressed (text alignment), with type="multiple" several (bold, italic, underline). The group is one tab stop; arrow keys move between items.
whenToUse: For related formatting or view options in an editor or toolbar.
For a compact single choice that should look like pressed buttons.
whenNotToUse: For a group of independent actions: use ButtonGroup.
For switching between views or modes of the page: use SegmentControl or Tabs.
do: Name the group with aria-label ("Text alignment").
Give icon-only items an aria-label each.
Use type="single" when the options exclude each other.
dont: Don't mix actions and toggles in one group.
Don't make groups longer than about five items.
accessibility: One tab stop; Left/Right (or Up/Down when vertical) and Home/End move focus.
Items announce aria-pressed (multiple) or act as radio items (single).
components.ai: With Pada, add a ToggleGroup type="single" aria-label="Text alignment" with icon-only items Left, Center, Right and Justify, bound to the paragraph's alignment.

components.name: Autocomplete
components.summary: A text field with filtered suggestions; pick one or several.
components.overview: Autocomplete is a combobox: people type to narrow a list of options, move with the arrow keys and press Enter to pick. With multiple, picks become chips and Backspace in the empty input removes the last one.
whenToUse: When the list is long (countries, people, repositories) and typing is faster than scrolling.
For picking several known values, such as assignees or labels (multiple).
whenNotToUse: For a short list (under about 10 options): use Select or RadioGroup.
For free-form values that are not in a list: use TagInput.
For searching content on a page: use SearchField.
do: Give it a visible label; use the placeholder only for an example.
Set an emptyMessage that helps ("No people match 'ana'").
Pass a custom filter when matching should use more than the label (email, aliases).
dont: Don't load thousands of options at once; filter on the server with onInputValueChange.
Don't let free text submit as if it were a picked option.
accessibility: WAI-ARIA combobox with a listbox popup; focus stays in the input and options are referenced with aria-activedescendant.
Arrow keys move, Enter picks, Escape closes; chips in multiple mode are removable from the keyboard.
components.ai: With Pada, add an Autocomplete labelled "Assignees" with multiple selection over the team members (value = user id, label = name), an empty message "No one matches", and bind the selected ids to the task form.

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: A single on/off choice, with a mixed state for "select all".
components.overview: Checkbox is a native checkbox with Pada's styles and an optional label. It supports an indeterminate (mixed) state for parent boxes that control a set. In Angular it works with forms as a boolean.
whenToUse: To accept a single statement: "I agree to the terms".
For independent options in a list, where any number can be on.
In table rows for selection.
whenNotToUse: For a setting that takes effect immediately: use Switch.
When only one option can be chosen: use RadioGroup.
For a labelled set with Select all: use CheckboxGroup.
do: Write labels as positive statements ("Email me updates", not "Don't email me").
Use indeterminate for a parent box when only some children are checked.
Put the label to the right of the box and make it clickable.
dont: Don't use a checkbox to trigger an action immediately.
Don't pre-check consent boxes.
accessibility: Native <input type="checkbox">; Space toggles it.
Indeterminate maps to aria-checked="mixed".
Inside a Field, the input takes the field's description and error.
components.ai: With Pada, add a required Checkbox "I agree to the terms of service" under the sign-up form, with a Field error "You need to accept the terms" when the form is submitted unchecked.

components.name: CheckboxGroup
components.summary: A labelled set of checkboxes with an optional Select all.
components.overview: CheckboxGroup renders options as checkboxes under one label and description. Its value is the array of checked option values, in option order. selectAll adds a parent box that turns mixed while only some are checked and only changes enabled choices.
whenToUse: For a set of related, independent options: notification topics, permissions, filters.
When people often want all or none (selectAll).
whenNotToUse: When exactly one option can be chosen: use RadioGroup.
For a long list of options: use Autocomplete with multiple.
do: Label the group with what is being chosen ("Notify me about").
Keep the list short and in a meaningful order.
Show a group-level error when a minimum selection is required.
dont: Don't nest groups more than one level.
Don't use a group for options that depend on each other.
accessibility: role="group" named by the label and described by the description and error.
Each choice is a native checkbox: Tab moves between them, Space toggles.
components.ai: With Pada, render a CheckboxGroup labelled "Notify me about" with options Comments, Mentions, Assignments and Weekly summary, a Select all box and the description "We send at most one email a day."

components.name: ColorPicker
components.summary: Pick a colour in OKLCH with an area, a hue slider, a hex field and swatches.
components.overview: ColorPicker works in OKLCH, the perceptual colour space Pada's tokens use. It has a 2D area for chroma and lightness, a hue slider, a hex field and optional swatches. Colours outside sRGB show at their nearest displayable colour. The value can be hex or OKLCH (format).
whenToUse: For brand or theme colours, tags and labels with custom colours.
Together with Pada's custom accent (data-accent="custom" and --pada-accent-hue).
whenNotToUse: When a fixed palette is enough: offer RadioCardGroup or swatches only.
do: Provide swatches for the colours people use most (brand colours).
Check contrast when a picked colour is used for text or controls.
Store OKLCH when you will derive tints from the colour.
dont: Don't use a colour picker as the only way to tell items apart; add names or icons.
accessibility: The area is a 2D slider: arrows change chroma and lightness (Shift ×10), PageUp/PageDown lightness, Home/End chroma. The hue is a standard slider.
The hex field commits on Enter or blur and reverts on Escape; it is aria-invalid while it holds text that is not a colour.
components.ai: With Pada, add a ColorPicker labelled "Accent colour" with swatches for our brand colours. When the value changes, set data-accent="custom" and --pada-accent-hue on the preview container so every component re-themes.

components.name: ComboBox
components.summary: A listbox of selectable options, used inside filters and custom pickers.
components.overview: ComboBox is a list of selectable options (role="listbox") with icons and single or multiple selection. On its own it manages focus with the arrow keys; inside a combobox it is driven through aria-activedescendant. Pada's toolbar filters are built on it.
whenToUse: As the option list inside a popover, filter chip or custom picker.
When you need the list behaviour without a text field.
whenNotToUse: For a form field: use Select (one value) or Autocomplete (typing to filter).
do: Give each item a short, scannable label and an optional icon.
Use multiSelect with a clear Apply or Clear pattern (see the Toolbar filters).
dont: Don't put actions in the list; use a DropdownMenu for actions.
accessibility: role="listbox" with role="option" items and aria-selected.
One tab stop; arrow keys, Home and End move between options.
components.ai: With Pada, build a "Status" filter popover whose content is a ComboBox with multiSelect over Open, In progress and Done, staging the selection until Apply is pressed.

components.name: Field
components.summary: Label, control, description and error, wired together for assistive technology.
components.overview: Field is the building block for form rows. Field.Root (or ds-field) generates the ids and wires the label, the control, the description and the error together, and carries invalid, required and disabled to every part. Use it for any control, including your own.
whenToUse: When you compose a custom control (a third-party input, a native select) and want Pada's label, help and error.
When you need a layout the all-in-one inputs don't offer.
whenNotToUse: For a standard text input: InputText already includes the label, description and error.
do: Write labels as nouns ("Email"), and put rules in the description ("At least 8 characters").
Write errors that say how to fix the problem ("Enter an email like name@example.com").
Mark optional fields when most are required, or required ones when most are optional, not both.
dont: Don't use placeholder text as the label.
Don't show an error before the person has had a chance to type.
accessibility: The label is a <label for>; the control gets aria-describedby for the description and error, and aria-invalid while invalid.
The required asterisk is hidden from screen readers because the control itself is required.
components.ai: With Pada, wrap our third-party phone input in a Field with the label "Phone number", the description "We'll text a code to this number." and an error from the form's validation, using Field.Control asChild (React) or dsInput inside ds-field (Angular).

components.name: InputText
components.summary: A labelled text input with description, error and prefix or suffix.
components.overview: InputText is the standard single-line text field: label, input, optional description, error and prefix or suffix content ("$", "kg", an icon). It accepts every native input attribute (type, autoComplete, inputMode). In Angular it works with forms and shows error once the control is invalid and touched.
whenToUse: For short free text: names, emails, URLs, titles.
whenNotToUse: For long text: use InputTextArea.
For numbers with steppers or formatting: use NumberInput.
For passwords: use PasswordInput. For search: use SearchField.
do: Set type and autoComplete so browsers and password managers help ("email", "name").
Size the field to the expected input length.
Use a prefix or suffix for units and currency instead of putting them in the label.
dont: Don't rely on the placeholder for instructions; it disappears when typing starts.
Don't validate on every keystroke; validate on blur or submit.
accessibility: The label is programmatically linked; description and error are in aria-describedby; aria-invalid is set while there is an error.
components.ai: With Pada, build a profile form with InputText fields Full name (autocomplete="name") and Email (type="email", autocomplete="email", required) with validation errors shown on blur.

components.name: InputTextArea
components.summary: A labelled multi-line text field.
components.overview: InputTextArea is a multi-line text field with Pada's label, description and error. Use it for comments, descriptions and notes.
whenToUse: For text that can run to several sentences: descriptions, feedback, messages.
whenNotToUse: For a single line: use InputText.
For rich text with formatting: use a dedicated editor and wrap it in a Field.
do: Make the starting height match the expected length.
Show a character limit in the description and count as people type when there is one.
dont: Don't use it for structured data that could be separate fields.
accessibility: A native <textarea> linked to its label, description and error.
components.ai: With Pada, add an InputTextArea labelled "Feedback" with the description "Max 500 characters", marked optional, and show an error when the text is longer than 500 characters.

components.name: NumberInput
components.summary: A number field with steppers, keyboard stepping and locale formatting.
components.overview: NumberInput is a spinbutton: type a value, use Up/Down, PageUp/PageDown and Home/End, or press and hold the steppers. Values are formatted with formatOptions (currency, percent, units) and typed text is parsed in the same locale.
whenToUse: For quantities, prices, percentages and limits with a known range.
whenNotToUse: For identifiers that look like numbers (phone numbers, card numbers, ZIP codes): use InputText.
For picking a rough value in a range: use Slider.
do: Set min, max and step to the real limits.
Use formatOptions for currency and units rather than putting symbols in the label.
dont: Don't use it for very large ranges where stepping is pointless; hide the steppers.
accessibility: WAI-ARIA Spinbutton: aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and a readable aria-valuetext with the formatted value.
components.ai: With Pada, add a NumberInput labelled "Seats" with min 1, max 500, step 1, and another labelled "Monthly budget" formatted as USD currency with no decimals.

components.name: PasswordInput
components.summary: A password field with show/hide and an optional strength meter.
components.overview: PasswordInput adds a show/hide toggle to a password field and an optional strength meter. It defaults to autoComplete="current-password"; set "new-password" on sign-up and change forms.
whenToUse: For sign-in, sign-up and password change forms.
whenNotToUse: For one-time codes: use PinInput.
do: Use autoComplete="new-password" when creating a password so password managers can suggest one.
Explain the rules in the description before people type.
Show strength while typing on sign-up; don't on sign-in.
dont: Don't block paste.
Don't show the password by default.
accessibility: The toggle is a button named "Show password" with aria-pressed, controlling the input.
The strength meter shows a text label next to the bar, so strength is not shown by colour alone.
components.ai: With Pada, build a sign-up password field with PasswordInput labelled "Password", autocomplete="new-password", a strength meter, and the description "At least 12 characters."

components.name: PinInput
components.summary: A code or PIN field with one box per character.
components.overview: PinInput collects short codes: verification codes, PINs. Typing moves to the next box, Backspace goes back, and pasting (or a phone autofilling a code from a text message) fills every box. groupSize splits long codes visually.
whenToUse: For one-time verification codes and short numeric PINs.
whenNotToUse: For passwords or long tokens: use PasswordInput or InputText.
do: Say where the code was sent in the description ("Sent to •••• 1234").
Submit automatically when the last box is filled, and offer "Resend code".
Keep one-time-code mode on (otp, the default) so phones can fill the code from a text message.
dont: Don't clear the code on error without explanation.
accessibility: Each box is labelled with its position ("Character 2 of 6"); the group is labelled by the field label.
Paste works from any box.
components.ai: With Pada, show a PinInput labelled "Verification code" with 6 digits, the description "We sent a code to ada@example.com", auto-submit when complete and an error "That code didn't work" on failure.

components.name: RadioCardGroup
components.summary: A single choice presented as rich cards.
components.overview: RadioCardGroup presents a single choice as cards with a title, description, icon and extra content: plans, shipping speeds, templates. It is built on native radios, so it submits with forms and behaves like any radio group.
whenToUse: When each option needs explanation or a price to choose well.
For a small number of options (two to six) that deserve visual weight.
whenNotToUse: For short, simple options: use RadioGroup.
For switching views: use SegmentControl or Tabs.
do: Keep card content parallel: the same fields in the same order.
Use columns to lay cards out in a grid; one column on small screens.
Preselect the recommended option when there is one.
dont: Don't put links or buttons inside a card; the whole card is the choice.
accessibility: Native radio inputs: Tab reaches the group, arrow keys move and select.
The title names each radio and the description is announced with it.
components.ai: With Pada, render a RadioCardGroup labelled "Plan" with three options (Starter, Team, Business), each with a title, a price in meta and a one-line description, in three columns, Team preselected.

components.name: RadioGroup
components.summary: A single choice from a short list.
components.overview: RadioGroup is a labelled set of native radio buttons for picking exactly one option. Tab reaches the group, arrow keys move and select, and the value submits with native forms.
whenToUse: For two to about six mutually exclusive options that should all be visible.
whenNotToUse: For many options: use Select.
For options that need descriptions and prices: use RadioCardGroup.
For a binary on/off: use Switch or Checkbox.
do: Order options logically (by frequency, size or time).
Set a sensible default when one exists.
Keep labels short and parallel.
dont: Don't use radios for actions; selecting a radio should never navigate or submit.
accessibility: role="radiogroup" named by the label; native radios give arrow-key navigation.
components.ai: With Pada, add a RadioGroup labelled "Delivery" with options Standard, Express and Pick up in store, defaulting to Standard, bound to the checkout form.

components.name: RangeSlider
components.summary: A slider with two thumbs for picking a range.
components.overview: RangeSlider picks a low and a high value: price, size, duration. Each thumb is a slider in its own right; pressing the track moves the nearest thumb. Values can be formatted with formatOptions.
whenToUse: For filters with a numeric range where approximate values are fine.
whenNotToUse: When exact numbers matter: use two NumberInputs (or pair them with the slider).
For date ranges: use DateRangePicker.
do: Show the current values (showValue) and format them (currency, units).
Name the thumbs with thumbLabels ("Minimum price", "Maximum price").
Use minStepsBetweenThumbs to stop the thumbs crossing.
dont: Don't use a step so small that the thumbs are hard to place.
accessibility: Two role="slider" thumbs with their own labels and value text.
Arrow keys step, PageUp/PageDown take ten steps, Home/End jump as far as the other thumb allows.
components.ai: With Pada, add a RangeSlider labelled "Price" from 0 to 1000 in steps of 10, formatted as USD, thumb labels "Minimum price" and "Maximum price", that filters the product list on commit.

components.name: Rating
components.summary: A star rating, interactive or read-only.
components.overview: Rating shows or collects a score out of max stars. Interactive ratings are a radio group (hover previews, the value submits with forms, allowClear lets people remove their rating); read-only ratings are a single image named like "4.5 out of 5 stars".
whenToUse: To collect quick satisfaction feedback.
To display an average score next to reviews.
whenNotToUse: For precise scores or scales with meaning per step: use RadioGroup with labelled options.
do: Show the number and the count of ratings next to a read-only rating ("4.5 · 120 reviews").
Label interactive ratings with the question ("Rate your experience").
dont: Don't use stars for things that aren't quality judgements.
accessibility: Interactive: a radio group; Tab in, arrow keys change the value.
Read-only: role="img" with a text alternative.
components.ai: With Pada, add an interactive Rating labelled "Rate your experience" (max 5, allowClear) to the feedback form, and show a readOnly Rating with the product's average next to its title.

components.name: SearchField
components.summary: A compact search input with an icon and a clear button.
components.overview: SearchField is a compact input with a leading search icon and a clear button that appears once there is text. Use it to filter lists and tables in place.
whenToUse: Above a list or table to filter it.
In headers and sidebars for searching a section.
whenNotToUse: For app-wide navigation and actions: use CommandPalette.
For picking a value from a list: use Autocomplete.
do: Give it an accessible name (aria-label="Search members") when there is no visible label.
Filter as people type (debounced) and show the result count.
Use a placeholder that says what is searched ("Search members").
dont: Don't clear the query when the results update.
accessibility: A labelled input (named "Search" unless you pass aria-label); the clear button is named "Clear search".
In Angular, Escape clears too and focus returns to the input.
components.ai: With Pada, add a SearchField with aria-label "Search members" above the members table that filters rows by name or email (debounced 200ms) and announces the result count.

components.name: SegmentControl
components.summary: A compact single choice between a few views or modes.
components.overview: SegmentControl is a row of segments for switching between a few views or modes: List / Board, Day / Week / Month. Selection follows focus.
whenToUse: To switch how the same content is shown.
For two to five short options.
whenNotToUse: For panels with different content: use Tabs.
For a form choice that is submitted: use RadioGroup.
do: Name it with aria-label ("View").
Keep labels to one or two words; give icon-only segments an ariaLabel.
dont: Don't use more than five segments.
Don't trigger slow loads on every arrow press; selection follows focus.
accessibility: role="tablist" with role="tab" segments; arrow keys move and select, skipping disabled ones.
components.ai: With Pada, add a SegmentControl aria-label="View" with options List and Board (with icons) above the tasks, switching the layout between a Table and a board.

components.name: Select
components.summary: A labelled dropdown for picking one option from a list.
components.overview: Select is a select-only combobox: focus stays on the trigger while the arrow keys, Home/End and type-ahead move through options. The list renders in a portal, flips above the trigger when there is no room and matches the trigger's width.
whenToUse: For one choice from about five to 15 options.
When space is limited and the options don't need to be compared side by side.
whenNotToUse: For a few options that should all be visible: use RadioGroup.
For long lists: use Autocomplete so people can type.
do: Use a placeholder such as "Choose a role" when there is no sensible default.
Order options alphabetically or by frequency.
Keep option labels short; put detail in the description of the field.
dont: Don't use Select for actions; use a DropdownMenu.
Don't auto-submit on change.
accessibility: WAI-ARIA select-only combobox: Enter, Space, ArrowDown open the list; type-ahead jumps to options; Escape closes and returns to the trigger.
components.ai: With Pada, add a Select labelled "Role" with options Admin, Editor and Viewer, a placeholder "Choose a role", required, bound to the invite form.

components.name: Slider
components.summary: A labelled single-value slider.
components.overview: Slider picks one value from a range by dragging or with the keyboard: volume, opacity, zoom. It has a label, an optional live value, a description and an error.
whenToUse: For approximate values where immediate feedback helps (preview updates as it moves).
whenNotToUse: For exact values: use NumberInput.
For a range: use RangeSlider.
do: Show the value (showValue) when the number matters.
Use sensible min, max and step.
dont: Don't use a slider without a label; pass aria-label if there is no visible one.
accessibility: Arrow keys step, PageUp/PageDown take ten steps, Home/End jump to the limits.
React uses a native range input; Angular uses a role="slider" thumb with the same keyboard map.
components.ai: With Pada, add a Slider labelled "Volume" from 0 to 100 with showValue, updating the audio player's volume as it moves.

components.name: Switch
components.summary: An on/off switch for settings that take effect immediately.
components.overview: Switch is a native checkbox with role="switch". Use it for settings that apply as soon as they change. loading shows a spinner in the knob and blocks interaction while a change saves.
whenToUse: For preferences and feature flags that save instantly: "Email notifications".
whenNotToUse: When the change only applies after Save: use Checkbox.
For formatting in an editor: use Toggle.
do: Label the setting, not the state: "Email notifications", not "On".
Use loading while a server-side change saves, and revert with an error if it fails.
dont: Don't use a switch in a form with a submit button.
accessibility: role="switch" with aria-checked; Space toggles it. loading sets aria-busy.
components.ai: With Pada, add a Switch labelled "Email notifications" in settings that saves immediately, shows loading while the request is pending and reverts with a danger toast on failure.

components.name: TagInput
components.summary: Free-form tags typed into one field.
components.overview: TagInput collects free-form values as tags: emails, keywords, labels. Enter or a comma adds the text as a tag; pasting a list adds them all. validate, maxTags and allowDuplicates control what is accepted.
whenToUse: For lists of values people type: email recipients, keywords.
whenNotToUse: When values come from a known list: use Autocomplete with multiple.
do: Validate each tag (validate) and explain rejected input in the error.
Use addOnBlur so typed text isn't lost when people move on.
Set separators to match the data (commas, spaces, new lines).
dont: Don't accept duplicates unless they mean something.
accessibility: Backspace in the empty field moves to the tags; Backspace or Delete removes one; arrow keys move between tags. Each tag's remove button is named "Remove <tag>".
components.ai: With Pada, add a TagInput labelled "Invite by email" that validates each tag as an email, allows up to 20, adds on blur, and shows an error for invalid addresses.

components.name: UploadField
components.summary: A file picker with a drop zone and a list of files with progress.
components.overview: UploadField is a drop zone backed by a real file input. Picked and dropped files list below with their size, upload progress, status and View / Remove actions. accept, maxFiles and maxSize constrain what is allowed.
whenToUse: For attaching documents and images to a record or message.
whenNotToUse: For a single avatar image with cropping: build a dedicated picker.
do: State accepted types and the size limit in the description ("PDF or PNG, up to 10 MB").
Show per-file progress and a clear error for rejected files.
Let people remove a file before submitting.
dont: Don't rely on drag and drop only; the zone is also a button that opens the file browser.
accessibility: The zone is a native file input: Tab to it, Space or Enter to browse.
File statuses and errors are announced.
components.ai: With Pada, add an UploadField labelled "Attachments" accepting PDF and PNG up to 10 MB, multiple, max 5 files, uploading each file on add and showing its progress and status.

components.name: Calendar
components.summary: A month grid for picking a day or a range.
components.overview: Calendar is a keyboard-navigable month grid for picking a day or a range. It can show several months side by side (numberOfMonths), mark today, and limit the selectable days. Compose your own header from Calendar.Root, Calendar.PrevButton, Calendar.Heading, Calendar.NextButton and Calendar.Grid.
whenToUse: Inline, when the calendar is the main content (booking, scheduling).
As the building block for custom date pickers.
whenNotToUse: In a form field: use InputDate or DateRangePicker, which open the calendar in a popover.
For dates far in the past (birthdays): let people type the date.
do: Set min / max and isDateUnavailable so days that can't be picked are disabled, rather than rejected later.
Use weekStartsOn to match the locale.
Show two months for ranges that often cross a month boundary.
dont: Don't rely on colour alone to show availability; disable or label the days.
accessibility: WAI-ARIA date grid. Arrow keys move by day and week, Home/End to the week's ends, PageUp/PageDown by month (Shift: by year), Enter or Space picks. Focus starts on the selected day, or today.
components.ai: With Pada, render an inline Calendar with two months side by side for picking a stay (range), weeks starting on Monday, and past days disabled.

components.name: DatePicker
components.summary: The date picker panel: days, months and years.
components.overview: DatePicker is the panel behind InputDate: a Calendar day grid whose month heading opens a month view and whose year opens a year view, for quick jumps. In React it is exported as DatePickerDropdown.
whenToUse: When you build your own trigger or field and need the full picker panel.
whenNotToUse: In a standard form: use InputDate, which wraps this panel in a field and popover.
For a plain month grid: use Calendar.
do: Limit the range with minDate and maxDate.
Return focus to the field that opened the panel when it closes.
dont: Don't show the panel permanently in a form; it takes a lot of space.
accessibility: Days use the Calendar keyboard (arrows, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown); month and year views are keyboard-navigable grids too.
components.ai: With Pada, open the DatePicker panel in a Popover from a custom "Due date" chip, and set the task's due date when a day is picked.

components.name: DateRangePicker
components.summary: A field that opens a two-month range calendar with optional presets.
components.overview: DateRangePicker is a field showing the chosen range that opens a two-month range calendar (and optional presets, such as Last 7 days) in a popover dialog. The first click picks the start and the second the end; the value only changes once both ends are picked.
whenToUse: For report periods, stays and any start/end pair of dates.
whenNotToUse: For a single date: use InputDate.
do: Offer presets for common periods in reports and dashboards.
Set minDate for future-only ranges (bookings) and isDateUnavailable for blocked days.
Match weekStartsOn to the locale.
dont: Don't use two separate date fields when the range is one concept.
accessibility: The field is a button; the popover is a dialog. Picking the end (or a preset) closes it and returns focus to the field; Escape closes it and keeps the previous range.
The calendar keyboard is Calendar's, crossing from one month's grid to the other.
components.ai: With Pada, add a DateRangePicker labelled "Report period" with presets Last 7 days, Last 30 days and This quarter, weeks starting Monday, that refetches the dashboard when the range changes.

components.name: InputDate
components.summary: A date field that opens the date picker in a popover.
components.overview: InputDate is a form field: a button showing the chosen date (or range with selection="range") that opens the date picker in a popover. Focus moves to the selected day; Escape closes the picker and returns to the field.
whenToUse: For dates in forms: due dates, start dates, appointments.
whenNotToUse: For start/end ranges where both ends must be picked together: use DateRangePicker.
For birthdays and other far-away dates: a typed date is faster.
do: Label with what the date means ("Due date"), not "Date".
Show the date in the locale's format.
Restrict the range with minDate and maxDate.
dont: Don't open the picker on page load.
accessibility: The field is a button that announces the current value; the popover is a dialog with the Calendar keyboard.
components.ai: With Pada, add an InputDate labelled "Due date" to the task form, with past dates disabled and an error "Pick a due date" when it is empty on submit.

components.name: TimePicker
components.summary: A time-of-day field in spinbutton segments, ordered by the locale.
components.overview: TimePicker is a labelled field of segments (hours, minutes, optional seconds, and AM/PM on a 12-hour clock) in the locale's order. The value is a 24-hour "HH:mm" (or "HH:mm:ss") string, null until every segment is filled. There is no dropdown: the segments are the whole control.
whenToUse: For times of day: meeting start, reminder time, opening hours.
whenNotToUse: For durations: use NumberInput with units.
do: Use minuteStep (for example 15) when only some minutes make sense.
Set min / max for business hours; out-of-range values mark the field invalid.
Leave hourCycle to the locale unless your product has a fixed convention.
dont: Don't ask for seconds unless they matter (granularity="second").
accessibility: Each segment is a spinbutton: ArrowUp/Down step, PageUp/PageDown by a larger step, Home/End to the ends, digits type in, A/P set AM/PM, ArrowLeft/Right move between segments.
components.ai: With Pada, add a TimePicker labelled "Start time" with minuteStep 15, min "08:00" and max "18:00", bound to the meeting form as an "HH:mm" string.

components.name: AlertDialog
components.summary: A modal confirmation that the person must answer before continuing.
components.overview: AlertDialog interrupts to ask for a decision: "Delete this project?" It is role="alertdialog", doesn't close on a click outside, and starts focus on Cancel, the safe choice. Compose it with AlertDialog.Title, Description, Cancel and Action.
whenToUse: Before destructive or irreversible actions: delete, revoke, discard unsaved changes.
whenNotToUse: For tasks with fields: use Dialog.
For information that doesn't need a decision: use Alert or a toast.
For reversible actions: do them and offer Undo in a toast instead.
do: Phrase the title as a question that names the thing: "Delete 'Q3 report'?"
Say what happens in the description ("This can't be undone").
Label the action with the verb ("Delete"), using the destructive variant.
dont: Don't use "OK" / "Cancel"; say exactly what the button does.
Don't ask for confirmation on routine actions; people stop reading.
accessibility: role="alertdialog" named by the title and described by the description; focus starts on Cancel.
Escape cancels; a click outside does not close it.
components.ai: With Pada, when the user clicks "Delete project", open an AlertDialog titled "Delete 'Q3 report'?" with the description "The project and its tasks are deleted for everyone. This can't be undone." and buttons Cancel and Delete (destructive). Only delete after Delete is pressed.

components.name: CommandPalette
components.summary: A searchable list of actions in a dialog, opened with ⌘K.
components.overview: CommandPalette is a keyboard-first launcher: press ⌘K (Ctrl+K), type to filter commands with fuzzy, ranked matching, use the arrows and press Enter to run. Commands have a label, a group, keywords, an icon and an optional shortcut.
whenToUse: In apps with many pages and actions, for power users and fast navigation.
whenNotToUse: As the only way to reach features; the palette complements visible navigation.
For filtering a single list: use SearchField.
do: Group commands (Navigation, Create, Settings) and add keywords for synonyms.
Show shortcuts so people learn them.
Advertise the hotkey in the UI (a search button with a Kbd hint).
dont: Don't run destructive commands without confirmation.
accessibility: A modal dialog with a combobox and a listbox; the active option is referenced with aria-activedescendant. Escape closes and restores focus.
components.ai: With Pada, add a CommandPalette (hotkey ⌘K) with groups Navigation (Dashboard, Projects, Settings), Create (New project, Invite member) and Theme (Light, Dark), each command with an icon and keywords, wired to the router and actions.

components.name: ContextMenu
components.summary: A menu opened at the pointer with right-click or a long press.
components.overview: ContextMenu is the same menu as DropdownMenu, opened at the pointer from a ContextMenu.Trigger area with right-click, Shift+F10 or a long press. It supports the same items, groups and submenus.
whenToUse: For shortcuts on canvases, file lists and editors where right-click is expected.
whenNotToUse: As the only way to reach an action: also offer a visible button or DropdownMenu.
do: Mirror the most common actions available elsewhere.
Keep it short and ordered by frequency.
dont: Don't override the browser's context menu on ordinary text and links.
accessibility: Opens with Shift+F10 or the Menu key from the focused trigger area; keyboard navigation is DropdownMenu's.
components.ai: With Pada, wrap each file row in a ContextMenu.Trigger with items Open, Rename, Move to… (submenu of folders) and Delete, matching the row's DropdownMenu.

components.name: Dialog
components.summary: A modal window for focused tasks that sit on top of the page.
components.overview: Dialog is a modal panel with a backdrop: edit a profile, create a project, review details. Compose Dialog.Root, Dialog.Trigger and Dialog.Content with Header, Title, Description, Body, Footer and CloseButton. It animates in and out, traps focus, locks page scroll and restores focus to the trigger when it closes.
whenToUse: For short, focused tasks that need the person's full attention: a form, a review step.
When the task can be completed or cancelled without leaving the page.
whenNotToUse: For confirming a destructive action: use AlertDialog.
For long or multi-step flows: use a page, or a Drawer that keeps context visible.
For light, non-blocking content next to a trigger: use Popover.
do: Always include a Dialog.Title; add a Dialog.Description when the purpose isn't obvious.
Put the primary action last in the footer and label it with a verb ("Save changes").
Pick the smallest size that fits the content.
Keep the content short enough that the body rarely scrolls.
dont: Don't open a dialog on page load or stack dialogs on top of each other.
Don't put a dialog's only close option in the footer; keep the close button and Escape.
accessibility: WAI-ARIA Dialog (Modal): role="dialog", aria-modal, named by the title and described by the description. The trigger gets aria-expanded and aria-controls.
Focus moves inside on open, Tab is trapped, Escape and the backdrop close it, and focus returns to the trigger.
components.ai: With Pada, add an "Edit profile" secondary Button that opens a small Dialog titled "Edit profile" with the description "Changes are visible to your team." Put Name and Email InputText fields in the body, and Cancel (secondary) and "Save changes" (primary, loading while saving) in the footer.

components.name: Drawer
components.summary: A dialog panel that slides in from an edge of the screen.
components.overview: Drawer is a modal panel that slides in from the left, right, top or bottom, with a backdrop. It uses the Dialog parts (Drawer.Header, Drawer.Title, Drawer.Body, Drawer.Footer) and comes in several sizes.
whenToUse: For details and edits that relate to the page underneath: a record's details, filters, settings.
For longer forms that would crowd a centred dialog.
whenNotToUse: For a short, focused task: use Dialog.
For mobile-first bottom panels with drag to close: use Sheet.
do: Open from the right for details and editing, from the left for navigation.
Keep the title visible and actions in the footer.
Size it to the content; avoid full-width drawers on desktop.
dont: Don't open a drawer from inside another drawer.
accessibility: Same as Dialog: role="dialog", focus trapped, Escape and the backdrop close it, focus returns to the trigger.
The slide motion is removed under reduced motion.
components.ai: With Pada, open a right-side Drawer titled "Order #4512" when a table row is clicked, showing the order in a DescriptionList, with Close and "Refund" buttons in the footer.

components.name: DropdownMenu
components.summary: A menu of actions or options opened from a button.
components.overview: DropdownMenu opens a list of actions from a trigger: row actions, account menus, "More" menus. It supports groups, labels, separators, checkbox and radio items, and nested submenus.
whenToUse: For a set of actions related to an object or a page.
For toggling a few view options (checkbox or radio items).
whenNotToUse: To pick a value in a form: use Select.
For actions on right-click: use ContextMenu (it shares the same parts).
For an app-level menu bar: use Menubar.
do: Start items with verbs and keep them short; show shortcuts on the right.
Group related items and separate destructive ones at the end.
Use submenus sparingly, one level deep.
dont: Don't hide the only way to do something important inside a menu.
Don't put form fields inside a menu.
accessibility: WAI-ARIA Menu Button. The trigger opens with click, Enter, Space, ArrowDown (first item) or ArrowUp (last item). Arrow keys, Home/End and type-ahead move; Escape closes and returns focus.
components.ai: With Pada, add a DropdownMenu to each card with an IconButton trigger "Card actions": Edit, Duplicate, a separator, then Delete. Delete opens an AlertDialog before deleting.

components.name: HoverCard
components.summary: A rich preview shown when hovering or focusing a link.
components.overview: HoverCard shows a preview of what a link points to: a profile, a page, a repository. It opens after a short delay on hover or keyboard focus and stays open while the pointer is over the card.
whenToUse: For optional previews that help people decide whether to follow a link.
whenNotToUse: For essential information or actions: they must be reachable through the link itself.
For a short label: use Tooltip.
do: Keep the card informational: an avatar, a name, a short bio, a few stats.
Make the trigger a real link to the full page.
dont: Don't put buttons or forms in a hover card.
accessibility: Opens on hover (not touch) and keyboard focus. The card is supplementary: touch and screen-reader users may never see it, so everything in it must also be available at the link's destination.
components.ai: With Pada, wrap each author name in a HoverCard whose trigger is a Link to the profile and whose content shows their Avatar, name, role and number of posts.

components.name: Popover
components.summary: A non-modal panel anchored to a trigger.
components.overview: Popover is a floating panel next to a trigger for light, interactive content: filters, a quick form, a colour picker. It closes on Escape, a click outside and when focus leaves it. Compose Popover.Root, Trigger, Content, Title, Arrow, Close and CloseButton; Popover.Anchor positions it against another element.
whenToUse: For small tasks related to the trigger that shouldn't block the page.
whenNotToUse: For a list of actions: use DropdownMenu.
For a short description on hover: use Tooltip.
For blocking tasks: use Dialog.
do: Give it a Popover.Title so it has a name.
Choose side and align so it doesn't cover what people are working on.
Keep the content small; move bigger tasks to a dialog or drawer.
dont: Don't open popovers on hover; use HoverCard for previews.
accessibility: The trigger gets aria-expanded and aria-controls; the content is named by its title.
Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. Positioning flips to stay on screen.
components.ai: With Pada, add a "Filters" secondary Button that opens a Popover (side bottom, align start) titled "Filters" with a Select for status and a Switch for "Only mine", and a close button.

components.name: Sheet
components.summary: A bottom sheet for mobile-first flows, with drag and snap points.
components.overview: Sheet is a dialog that rises from the bottom edge: filters, a share menu, details on mobile. Drag it down to close, or between snapPoints; Escape and the backdrop close it too. It uses the Dialog parts inside.
whenToUse: On small screens, for secondary tasks that should keep the page in view.
For pickers and action lists that are reached with the thumb.
whenNotToUse: On desktop layouts with room for a side panel: use Drawer or Dialog.
do: Give it a title even when it is visually short.
Use snap points for content that can be glanced at, then expanded.
Keep the primary action reachable without scrolling.
dont: Don't nest scrolling areas that fight with the drag gesture.
accessibility: A modal dialog: focus trapped, named by its title, Escape closes it. Drag is never the only way to close it.
components.ai: With Pada, on mobile show the product filters in a Sheet titled "Filters" with snap points at 50% and 90%, a CheckboxGroup for brands and a RangeSlider for price, and an "Apply" button.

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: A short description shown on hover and keyboard focus.
components.overview: Tooltip describes an element in a few words: an icon button's action, a truncated label, a keyboard shortcut. It opens on hover after a delay and immediately on keyboard focus. Tooltip.Provider shares delays so moving between triggers is instant.
whenToUse: To name icon-only controls and show their shortcuts.
To reveal the full text of truncated content.
whenNotToUse: For information people need to complete a task: put it on the page.
For interactive content: use Popover or HoverCard.
For help next to a label: use InfoTooltip.
do: Keep it to a few words, without a period.
Add the keyboard shortcut with Kbd when there is one.
dont: Don't put links or buttons in a tooltip.
Don't add tooltips to disabled elements; they can't be focused.
accessibility: WAI-ARIA Tooltip: the trigger gets aria-describedby while open; Escape, blur and pointer-down close it.
components.ai: With Pada, wrap the toolbar's icon buttons in Tooltips ("Bold ⌘B", "Italic ⌘I") inside one Tooltip.Provider so moving between them skips the delay.

components.name: Alert
components.summary: An inline, persistent message inside a page or form.
components.overview: Alert is a callout that stays in place until the situation changes: a failed payment, a form-level error, a heads-up before a destructive change. It comes in five tones (neutral, info, success, warning, danger), with an optional title, icon, actions and dismiss button.
whenToUse: For messages tied to a section of the page or a form.
When the message must stay visible until the person deals with it.
whenNotToUse: For a brief confirmation such as "Saved": use a Toaster toast.
For a site-wide promotion or announcement: use Banner.
When the person must decide before continuing: use AlertDialog.
do: Match the tone to the meaning: danger for failures, warning for risk, success for completion.
Lead with what happened in the title and say what to do next in the body.
Put the fixing action in the alert ("Update card").
Use live="assertive" only for urgent errors that appear after an action; polite for the rest.
dont: Don't stack several alerts in one place; combine them or prioritise.
Don't rely on colour alone; keep the icon and the title.
accessibility: Without live, the alert is static content. live="polite" gives it role="status", live="assertive" gives it role="alert", so screen readers announce it when it appears.
The dismiss button is a labelled native button.
components.ai: With Pada, show a danger Alert titled "Payment failed" above the billing form when the charge is declined, with the text "Check your card details and try again." and an "Update card" secondary small Button in its actions. Announce it assertively.

components.name: Banner
components.summary: A wide promotional or informational strip with a visual, text and an action.
components.overview: Banner is a full-width strip for announcements and nudges: "Invite your team", "New: dark mode", "Scheduled maintenance". It has an optional icon or image, a title, a subtitle and one action.
whenToUse: To announce a feature, an event or a recommended next step.
At the top of a dashboard or a list page.
whenNotToUse: For errors and warnings tied to content: use Alert.
For brief, transient feedback: use a Toaster toast.
do: Keep it to one message and one action.
Make the title short and the subtitle explain the benefit.
Let people dismiss promotional banners and remember the choice.
dont: Don't show more than one banner at a time.
Don't use a banner for critical errors; it reads as marketing.
accessibility: The title is a heading and the action is a real button or link.
Decorative visuals are hidden from assistive technology; pass alt text for meaningful images.
components.ai: With Pada, add a Banner at the top of the dashboard with the "team" icon, title "Invite your team", subtitle "Pada is better together." and a secondary "Invite" button that opens the invite dialog.

components.name: EmptyState
components.summary: A placeholder for first use, no results and errors, with a clear next step.
components.overview: EmptyState fills a region that has nothing to show yet: no projects, no search results, a failed load. It has a media slot (an icon or illustration), a title, a description and actions, in two sizes.
whenToUse: On first use, to explain what goes here and how to start.
When a search or filter returns nothing.
When content failed to load and can be retried.
whenNotToUse: While content is loading: use Skeleton or Spinner.
For page-level errors that need attention elsewhere: use Alert.
do: Say what is missing and why, then offer one primary action ("Create project").
For no results, show the query and offer to clear filters.
Use the small size inside cards and tables, the default size for whole pages.
dont: Don't leave a blank area or a bare "No data".
Don't offer more than two actions.
accessibility: The title renders as a heading (headingLevel), so it fits the page outline.
The media is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
components.ai: With Pada, when the projects list is empty, show an EmptyState with the "folder" icon, title "No projects yet", description "Create a project to start tracking work." and a primary "New project" button with an "add" icon.

components.name: Progress
components.summary: A progress bar for a task with a known (or unknown) amount of work.
components.overview: Progress shows how far a task has come: an upload, an import, a quota. It is a horizontal bar with a label; give it a value out of max. In Angular, value of null shows an indeterminate, sweeping bar.
whenToUse: For tasks longer than a couple of seconds where progress can be measured.
For usage against a limit (storage, seats), alongside the numbers.
whenNotToUse: In a tight space such as a table cell or a button: use ProgressCircle.
For short waits with no measurable progress: use Spinner.
do: Always give it a label that says what is progressing ("Uploading report.pdf").
Show the numbers next to the bar for quotas ("42 of 50 seats").
Move to a success state or message when the task completes.
dont: Don't let the bar go backwards or jump to 100% and sit there.
Don't use colour alone to show a quota is nearly full; add text.
accessibility: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax.
State is exposed as data-state for styling. The Angular bar is named by label; React and Angular differences are listed in each Storybook page.
components.ai: With Pada, show a Progress bar labelled "Uploading report.pdf" bound to the upload's percentage, and replace it with a success Alert when the upload finishes.

components.name: ProgressCircle
components.summary: A compact ring that fills with progress or spins while indeterminate.
components.overview: ProgressCircle is circular progress for compact places: a file row, a table cell, a button. It fills clockwise from the top for a known value, or spins while value is null. Three sizes, with an optional value label in the middle.
whenToUse: When there is no room for a bar: lists, cells, cards.
For per-item progress in a list of uploads or jobs.
whenNotToUse: When there is room for a bar and a label: use Progress.
For a generic page or section wait: use Spinner or Skeleton.
do: Name it with label ("Uploading report.pdf").
Use showValue on the large size when the percentage matters.
Keep sizes consistent within one list.
dont: Don't show several spinning rings at once for one task.
Don't use it as decoration.
accessibility: role="progressbar" named by label, with aria-valuenow (left out while indeterminate).
data-state is indeterminate, loading or complete.
components.ai: With Pada, add a small ProgressCircle to each row of the upload list, labelled with the file name and bound to that file's percentage; show it indeterminate until the first progress event.

components.name: Skeleton
components.summary: A shimmering placeholder that holds the shape of content while it loads.
components.overview: Skeleton draws the outline of content that is on its way: lines of text, a rectangle for an image, a circle for an avatar. It reduces layout shift and makes loading feel faster.
whenToUse: For the first load of a page, card or list whose layout you know.
When content takes more than a moment and will replace the placeholder in place.
whenNotToUse: For actions the person just started (saving, sending): use a Button loading state or Spinner.
When the load failed or returned nothing: use EmptyState.
do: Match the real layout: the same number of lines, avatar size and card height.
Use lines for text blocks; the last line is shorter, like real text.
Mark the loading region with aria-busy="true" and remove it when content arrives.
dont: Don't show skeletons for more than a few seconds without a fallback message.
Don't mix skeletons and spinners in the same region.
accessibility: Skeletons are hidden from assistive technology (aria-hidden). Announce loading through aria-busy on the region.
The shimmer stops under reduced motion.
components.ai: With Pada, while the team list loads, render five rows of Skeletons: a circle (40px) for the avatar and two text lines, inside a region with aria-busy="true" that is removed once the data arrives.

components.name: Spinner
components.summary: An indeterminate loading indicator.
components.overview: Spinner tells people something is happening when there is no measurable progress. It rotates, and under reduced motion it pulses slowly instead. Three sizes.
whenToUse: For short waits (a second or two) such as loading a popover or refreshing a panel.
Inline next to the thing that is loading.
whenNotToUse: For first page loads with a known layout: use Skeleton.
When progress is measurable: use Progress or ProgressCircle.
Inside a button: use the Button loading state.
do: Keep the default label ("Loading") or make it specific ("Loading comments").
Pass label={null} when the spinner sits inside something that already announces loading.
dont: Don't show a full-page spinner for content that could load progressively.
Don't leave a spinner running when a request fails; show an error.
accessibility: With a label, the spinner is role="status" with visually hidden text, so the label is announced.
The animation respects reduced motion.
components.ai: With Pada, show a small Spinner labelled "Loading comments" under the post while comments are fetched, then replace it with the comment list or an EmptyState.

components.name: Toaster
components.summary: Brief notifications created with toast(), stacked in a corner.
components.overview: Render one Toaster near the root of the app and call toast() (or toast.success, toast.info, toast.warning, toast.danger) from anywhere. Toasts stack in a corner, expand on hover or focus, pause their timers while hovered, focused or in a background tab, and can be swiped or Escaped away. In Angular, use ToastService (or injectToast()) the same way.
whenToUse: To confirm an action that happened: "Invite sent", "Changes saved".
For background events: "Export ready".
With an Undo action for reversible operations.
whenNotToUse: For errors that block progress or need a fix in a form: use Alert next to the problem.
For questions that need an answer: use AlertDialog.
do: Keep titles short and specific; add a description only when it helps.
Offer one action at most (Undo, View, Retry).
Use the danger tone for failures, and give toasts with an action a longer duration (the default is 5 seconds).
dont: Don't put essential information only in a toast; it disappears.
Don't fire several toasts for one action.
accessibility: The toaster is a labelled region ("Notifications (F8)"); F8 moves focus to it.
Toasts are announced politely (role="status"), danger toasts assertively; timers pause while focus is inside.
components.ai: With Pada, render a Toaster at the app root (bottom-right). After inviting a member, call toast.success with title "Invite sent", the email as description and an Undo action that cancels the invite.

components.name: Breadcrumbs
components.summary: Shows where the current page sits in the hierarchy.
components.overview: Breadcrumbs show the path from the top of the app to the current page: Projects › Q3 report › Settings. Long trails collapse in the middle (maxItems) behind a "…" button. renderLink (React) lets crumbs use your router.
whenToUse: In apps with more than two levels of hierarchy.
At the top of detail and settings pages, usually inside PageHeader.
whenNotToUse: In flat apps, or for step-by-step flows: use Steps.
do: Use page titles as labels, short and consistent with the navigation.
Make every crumb except the last a link; the last is the current page.
Collapse long trails, keeping the first and last crumbs.
dont: Don't use breadcrumbs to show history ("back" trail).
accessibility: WAI-ARIA Breadcrumb: a labelled nav with an ordered list; the current page has aria-current="page". Separators are hidden from assistive technology.
components.ai: With Pada, render Breadcrumbs for Projects › Q3 report › Settings with maxItems 3, using my router's Link through renderLink (React) or routerLink (Angular).

components.name: Indexer
components.summary: An "on this page" index that follows the reader.
components.overview: Indexer lists the sections of a long page and highlights the one being read. Clicking an entry scrolls its section into view (smoothly, unless the person prefers reduced motion). Sections are found by id; offset sets where a section becomes active.
whenToUse: On long documentation, settings and report pages with clear sections.
whenNotToUse: For switching between separate panels: use Tabs.
On short pages with two or three sections.
do: Use the section headings as labels.
Keep it sticky next to the content on wide screens; hide it on narrow ones.
dont: Don't nest more than one level of entries.
accessibility: A labelled navigation landmark; the active entry has aria-current.
components.ai: With Pada, add a sticky Indexer to the right of the settings page listing the sections Profile, Notifications, Security and Billing (by their heading ids).

components.name: Menubar
components.summary: A horizontal bar of menus, as in desktop applications.
components.overview: Menubar is a row of menu triggers (File, Edit, View) for editor-style apps. Each Menubar.Menu has a trigger and content built from the DropdownMenu item parts, including checkbox and radio items and submenus.
whenToUse: In document, design and data editors with many commands.
whenNotToUse: For site navigation: use Sidebar, Tabs or links.
For a few actions: use Toolbar or DropdownMenu.
do: Name the bar with aria-label ("Editor").
Follow platform conventions for menu names and order.
Show shortcuts next to items.
dont: Don't put navigation links in a menubar.
accessibility: WAI-ARIA Menubar: one tab stop; Left/Right move between menus, Down opens one; once a menu is open, Left/Right move to the neighbouring menu.
components.ai: With Pada, add a Menubar aria-label="Editor" with File (New, Open, Save ⌘S), Edit (Undo, Redo) and View (checkbox items Show grid and Show rulers) menus.

components.name: PageHeader
components.summary: The bar at the top of a page: breadcrumbs, search, AI and profile.
components.overview: PageHeader is the app's top bar: a breadcrumb trail on the left and, on the right, a command (search) button with its shortcut, an AI button and a profile button with a menu. Long trails collapse to the first and last crumbs.
whenToUse: At the top of every page in an app shell, next to a Sidebar.
whenNotToUse: For marketing pages: build a site header instead.
do: Wire the command button to a CommandPalette and show its shortcut.
Use the profile menu for account actions (Settings, Sign out).
dont: Don't put page-specific actions in the header; put them in the page or a Toolbar.
accessibility: The command and AI buttons are named by commandLabel and aiLabel.

In React, give a custom profileTrigger an accessible name (for example an Avatar image with alt text). Angular names the profile button with profileLabel and renders the trail as a labelled nav list with aria-current="page".
components.ai: With Pada, add a PageHeader with breadcrumbs from the current route, a command button (⌘K) that opens our CommandPalette, an AI button that opens the assistant panel, and a profile Avatar menu with Settings and Sign out.

components.name: Pagination
components.summary: Previous, numbered pages with ellipses, next.
components.overview: Pagination moves between pages of results. It shows previous and next buttons and page numbers with ellipses around the current page (siblingCount, boundaryCount).
whenToUse: Below lists and search results that are split into pages.
whenNotToUse: Inside tables with rows per page: use the Table's pagination footer (TablePagination).
For feeds: use infinite loading with a "Load more" button.
do: Keep it in the same place on every page.
Show the total count of results nearby.
Scroll to the top of the list when the page changes.
dont: Don't paginate fewer than about 25 items.
accessibility: A labelled nav; the current page has aria-current="page"; previous and next are named and disabled at the ends.
components.ai: With Pada, add Pagination under the search results (page from the URL, totalPages from the API, siblingCount 1) that updates the URL and scrolls to the top on change.

components.name: Pills
components.summary: A row of rounded, single-select pills for switching views or filters.
components.overview: Pills are rounded choices for switching quickly between views or filters: All, Open, Closed. They behave like tabs: arrow keys move and select, and only the selected pill is in the tab order.
whenToUse: For quick filters above a list or feed.
whenNotToUse: For panels with different content: use Tabs.
For many filters at once: use the Toolbar filters.
do: Keep labels to one or two words; add counts when helpful ("Open 12").
Default to the most useful option.
dont: Don't wrap pills onto several lines; scroll or reduce the options.
accessibility: A tab list: arrow keys and Home/End move and select, wrapping and skipping disabled pills.
components.ai: With Pada, add Pills with options All, Open and Closed above the issue list, filtering the list by status.

components.name: Sidebar
components.summary: The app's side navigation, from data, with sections, search and collapse.
components.overview: Sidebar is the app-shell navigation: a logo, a search, sections of menu items with icons and badges, nested items and a collapse toggle. Pass it data (or compose its parts) and the active id.
whenToUse: As the main navigation of an app with more than a handful of sections.
whenNotToUse: For in-page navigation: use Indexer or Tabs.
do: Group items into labelled sections and order them by frequency.
Keep labels short; use icons consistently across items.
Remember the collapsed state per person.
dont: Don't nest more than two levels.
accessibility: Rendered as an <aside>; the active item has aria-current="page" and the collapse toggle announces aria-expanded. Give the sidebar an aria-label ("Main navigation").
components.ai: With Pada, build the app Sidebar from data: our logo, a search, sections Workspace (Dashboard, Projects, Reports) and Settings (Team, Billing), with icons and the active item from the router.

components.name: Steps
components.summary: A vertical list of steps in a flow, with their status.
components.overview: Steps show progress through a multi-step flow: checkout, onboarding, setup. Each step has a title, a description and a status (completed, current, upcoming); completed and upcoming steps can be selected.
whenToUse: For flows of three to seven steps where people benefit from seeing what's next.
whenNotToUse: For a history of events: use Timeline.
For independent sections: use Tabs.
do: Name steps by their outcome ("Payment", "Review").
Let people go back to completed steps.
dont: Don't use more than about seven steps; group them.
accessibility: The current step has aria-current="step"; each step announces its status ("Plan (current step)").
components.ai: With Pada, add Steps for onboarding (Account, Workspace, Invite team, Done) bound to the current step, letting people go back to completed steps.

components.name: Tabs
components.summary: Tabbed sections that switch panels in place.
components.overview: Tabs organise related content into panels shown one at a time. Compose Tabs.Root, Tabs.List, Tabs.Trigger and Tabs.Content; choose a visual variant, horizontal or vertical orientation, and automatic or manual activationMode. A sliding indicator follows the selected tab.
whenToUse: To split a page into peer sections: Overview, Activity, Settings.
whenNotToUse: For steps in a sequence: use Steps.
To switch the view of the same data: use SegmentControl.
When people need to compare content side by side.
do: Keep labels short and use nouns.
Use activationMode="manual" when panels are slow to render.
Keep the selected tab in the URL for deep links.
dont: Don't nest tabs inside tabs.
Don't use tabs for navigation between pages; use links.
accessibility: WAI-ARIA Tabs: one tab stop for the list; arrow keys move, Home/End jump; panels are labelled by their tabs.
components.ai: With Pada, split the project page into Tabs (Overview, Activity, Settings) with the selected tab synced to the ?tab= query parameter.

components.name: Toolbar
components.summary: Filters and a view switcher on the left, actions on the right.
components.overview: Toolbar sits above lists and tables: filter chips and a view switcher on the left, buttons on the right (actions and a primaryAction). Pada's filters (Filter, MoreFilter, FilterChip) are built for it.
whenToUse: Above data views to filter, switch views and act on the data.
whenNotToUse: For editor formatting: use ToggleGroup inside a toolbar region.
For app-level menus: use Menubar.
do: Name it with aria-label ("Members").
Keep one primary action on the right ("Invite").
Use MoreFilter when filters don't fit as chips.
dont: Don't put more than three secondary actions; move the rest into a menu.
accessibility: In Angular, role="toolbar" with roving focus (one tab stop, Left/Right and Home/End). In React, a flex container whose buttons are separate tab stops; the difference is documented.
components.ai: With Pada, put a Toolbar above the members table with a Status Filter (Active, Invited, Suspended), a MoreFilter for Role and Team, an "Export" action and a primary "Invite" action.

components.name: DataTable
components.summary: A data-driven table with sorting, search, selection, column visibility and paging.
components.overview: DataTable turns data and columns into a full table: sortable headers, a search over searchable columns, row selection with a select-all box, a Columns menu, bulk actions and paging. Every piece of state can be controlled, or handed to a server with manual. The logic is also available without markup as useDataTable in pada-ds/headless.
whenToUse: For lists of records people scan, sort, filter and act on: users, orders, invoices.
whenNotToUse: For a small static table: use Table.
For a single record's fields: use DescriptionList.
do: Make the first column the row header (the name people recognise).
Align numbers to the right and format them; sort numbers and dates naturally.
Use manual with server-side sorting, search and paging for large data sets.
Show the selected count and bulk actions only while rows are selected.
dont: Don't show every field; hide less important columns by default.
Don't put more than one or two inline actions per row; use a row menu.
accessibility: Header buttons report aria-sort; the search result count is announced.
Row checkboxes are named by the row header; select-all goes mixed on a partial selection.
components.ai: With Pada, render the users as a DataTable with columns Name (row header, sortable), Email (searchable), Role and Last active (date, sortable), row selection with a "Remove" bulk action, 10 rows per page, and server-side paging through manual mode.

components.name: DescriptionList
components.summary: A record's attributes as sections of terms and values, from data.
components.overview: DescriptionList renders the fields of one record from data: sections with a header (tooltip, buttons, badges) and rows of terms and values. Values can be text, an avatar with a name, a badge, a button or custom content. Button presses come out of onAction.
whenToUse: On detail pages and drawers for a record: an order, a user, a policy.
whenNotToUse: For a single pair in a settings row: use KeyValue.
For many records: use Table or DataTable.
do: Group fields into sections with clear headers ("Ownership", "Billing").
Map your API response to the component's data shape in one adapter function.
Show an em dash for empty values rather than hiding the row.
dont: Don't use it for editable forms; switch to form fields when editing.
accessibility: Each section is a role="group" named by its header, holding a native dl with dt and dd.
components.ai: With Pada, show the order in a DescriptionList with sections Customer (name with avatar, email) and Status (a success badge "Paid", payment method), plus an "Edit" button in the section header handled by onAction. Write a toDescriptionListData(order) adapter.

components.name: Table
components.summary: Rows and cells with sortable, resizable and reorderable columns.
components.overview: Table is the presentational layer under DataTable: rows and cells on a CSS grid, with an optional toolbar above and pagination below. Column headers can sort, resize (drag the edge, or focus it and press Left/Right) and reorder (drag a header onto another).
whenToUse: When you need full control over rows and cells, or the data is small and static.
whenNotToUse: For typical record lists with sorting, search and selection: use DataTable.
do: Name the table with label or labelledBy.
Mark the identifying cell of each row as the row header.
Keep column widths stable as data loads.
dont: Don't use a table for layout.
accessibility: role="table" with rows, column headers and cells. Sortable headers report aria-sort; resize handles are focusable and keyboard-operable.
components.ai: With Pada, build a Table labelled "Invoices" with columns Number, Customer, Amount (right-aligned, currency) and Status (Badge), a sortable Amount header, and TablePagination below.

components.name: Timeline
components.summary: An ordered list of events joined by a line.
