components.overview: Timeline shows events in order: activity feeds, audit logs, order tracking. Each event has a marker, a title, a time and details. Events appear one after another on mount, and pending events are drawn hollow and dashed. A compact density suits sidebars.
whenToUse: For history and status over time.
whenNotToUse: For a flow the person is moving through: use Steps.
do: Order events consistently (newest first for feeds, oldest first for tracking).
Use relative times for recent events and absolute dates for older ones, with the full timestamp available.
Use tones on markers sparingly: success for completed, danger for failures.
dont: Don't load unbounded history; paginate or "Show more".
accessibility: An ordered list; times are <time> elements. The entry animation respects reduced motion.
components.ai: With Pada, show order tracking as a Timeline: Order placed, Payment confirmed, Shipped (completed), Out for delivery (pending), each with a time; map the API's events with a toTimelineData adapter.

components.name: Tree
components.summary: A tree of items for file browsers, navigation and nested settings.
components.overview: Tree shows hierarchical items that expand and collapse: folders and files, nested categories. Selection is single, multiple or none. Pass items, or compose Tree.Root, Tree.Item, Tree.ItemRow, Tree.ItemLabel and Tree.Group for custom rows.
whenToUse: For deep hierarchies people browse and select from.
whenNotToUse: For two-level navigation: use Sidebar sections.
For collapsible content sections: use Accordion.
do: Name the tree with aria-label ("Files").
Use icons to tell item types apart (folder, file).
Load children lazily for large trees.
dont: Don't put buttons inside rows; use a context menu or a row menu.
accessibility: WAI-ARIA Tree View: Up/Down move, Right expands or enters, Left collapses or goes up, Home/End jump, * expands siblings, typing jumps to an item.
components.ai: With Pada, render the project files as a Tree aria-label="Files" with single selection, folder and file icons, and open the selected file in the editor.

components.name: Accordion
components.summary: Collapsible sections that show one or several panels at a time.
components.overview: Accordion stacks sections whose content expands and collapses under a heading button. Compose Accordion.Root (type="single", optionally collapsible, or type="multiple"), Item, Trigger and Content; the content's height animates. <Accordion header> (React) or ds-accordion-section (Angular) is one standalone section.
whenToUse: For FAQs, settings groups and long pages where people scan headings first.
whenNotToUse: When people need to compare sections side by side: show them all.
For primary navigation: use Tabs or Sidebar.
do: Write headings that describe the content, so the collapsed list reads as a summary.
Use type="single" with collapsible for FAQs, multiple for settings.
Set headingLevel to fit the page outline.
dont: Don't hide critical information in a collapsed section.
Don't nest accordions.
accessibility: WAI-ARIA Accordion: each header is a button inside a heading with aria-expanded and aria-controls; arrow keys and Home/End move between headers.
components.ai: With Pada, render an FAQ as an Accordion type="single" collapsible with items "Is Pada free?", "Which browsers are supported?" and "Can I use my own styles?", headings at level 3.

components.name: Avatar
components.summary: A picture for a person or entity, with initials and status fallbacks.
components.overview: Avatar shows a person's or organisation's picture once it loads; until then (or if it fails) it shows initials on a colour derived from the name, or a person icon. Five sizes, circle or square shape, and an optional status dot (online, away, busy, offline). AvatarGroup overlaps several with a "+N" counter.
whenToUse: Next to names in lists, comments, assignees and headers.
whenNotToUse: For company or tool logos: use BrandLogo.
do: Always pass name, so the fallback and the accessible name work.
Use the square shape for organisations and workspaces.
Cap groups (for example at four) and show the rest as "+N".
dont: Don't rely on the status colour alone; show the status in text somewhere.
accessibility: With a picture, alt defaults to the name; next to a visible name, mark it decorative with an empty alt to avoid repetition.
components.ai: With Pada, show the task assignees as an AvatarGroup of small avatars (name and src from the API), capped at 4 with a "+N" counter, each wrapped in a Tooltip with the person's name.

components.name: Badge
components.summary: A short status label or a count.
components.overview: Badge labels status or shows a count: "Beta", "Overdue", "12". It comes in six tones (neutral, accent, success, warning, danger, info), subtle, solid or outline, two sizes, a count with max ("99+") and a dot mode.
whenToUse: For status in tables and cards, and counts on navigation items.
whenNotToUse: For removable or clickable labels: use Tags.
For important messages: use Alert.
do: Keep the text to one or two words.
Use tones consistently across the product (danger always means failed or overdue).
Use max so large counts don't break the layout.
dont: Don't use badges as buttons.
Don't use a dot without a text alternative nearby.
accessibility: Plain text, so it is read with its context; counts can be given a fuller label with aria-label ("12 unread messages").
components.ai: With Pada, show each invoice's status as a Badge: Paid (success), Due (warning), Overdue (danger), Draft (neutral), and an unread count Badge (max 99) on the Inbox sidebar item.

components.name: BrandLogo
components.summary: A third-party brand logo (Slack, GitHub, …) by name.
components.overview: BrandLogo renders a logo from Pada's library of third-party brands by name: integrations, connected accounts, sign-in providers. It has sizes, an optional background tile and a tooltip. In Angular, serve the logo images from your app (or point provideBrandLogoUrl elsewhere).
whenToUse: In integration lists, connected accounts and import sources.
whenNotToUse: For Pada's own logo: use PadaLogo.
For people: use Avatar.
do: Pair the logo with the brand's name in text.
Use the background tile when logos sit on varied surfaces.
dont: Don't recolour or distort brand logos.
accessibility: Decorative when the name is next to it; otherwise give it a text alternative.
components.ai: With Pada, list our integrations (Slack, GitHub, Jira) as rows with a BrandLogo (size lg, with background), the name and a Switch to connect each.

components.name: Card
components.summary: A bordered surface that groups related content.
components.overview: Card is a bordered, rounded surface for a self-contained piece of content: a summary, a plan, a project tile. It follows the theme's surface, border and radius tokens.
whenToUse: To group content that belongs together on dashboards and grids.
whenNotToUse: To wrap a whole page or every section; use spacing and headings instead.
For selectable options: use RadioCardGroup.
do: Give each card a heading and keep content parallel across a grid.
If the whole card is a link, make one link cover it rather than nesting several.
dont: Don't nest cards inside cards.
accessibility: A plain container; give it structure with headings. Use a list when cards are a collection.
components.ai: With Pada, render a Grid (minItemWidth 280px) of Cards for projects, each with a Heading level 3, a short description, a status Badge and an owner Avatar.

components.name: Carousel
components.summary: A rotating set of slides with controls.
components.overview: Carousel shows one slide at a time with previous/next buttons and dots. Auto-rotation (autoPlay) pauses while the pointer or keyboard focus is inside, can be paused with its rotation button and is off when the person prefers reduced motion.
whenToUse: For a few visual highlights, onboarding tips or image galleries where seeing all at once isn't needed.
whenNotToUse: For important content: people rarely see slides after the first.
For long lists: use a grid or a horizontal ScrollArea.
do: Keep it to three to five slides and name the carousel with label.
Make each slide make sense on its own.
dont: Don't auto-rotate slides that contain text people need to read.
accessibility: WAI-ARIA Carousel: slides are labelled "n of m"; the rotation control is a real button; rotation stops on focus and hover.
components.ai: With Pada, add a Carousel labelled "What's new" with three slides (image, heading, one line of text), showDots and showNav, without auto-play.

components.name: CodeSnippet
components.summary: A code block with a label, syntax highlighting and a copy button.
components.overview: CodeSnippet shows code on a dark surface with a label, syntax highlighting and a copy button. Types: micro (inline), single-line (a command) and multi-line (a block).
whenToUse: For install commands, API keys, configuration and code samples.
whenNotToUse: For keyboard shortcuts: use Kbd.
do: Set language for highlighting and a label that says what it is ("Install").
Keep single-line snippets copyable as-is: no prompts ($) inside the code.
dont: Don't show secrets in full; mask them and copy the real value.
accessibility: The copy button is a labelled button that changes to "Copied" after copying. In Angular, the code block is a focusable, named region so keyboard users can scroll it.
components.ai: With Pada, show the install step as a single-line CodeSnippet (language bash, label "Install") with "npm install pada-ds", and a multi-line TSX snippet below with the quick-start code.

components.name: Heading
components.summary: A native h1–h6 on the type scale.
components.overview: Heading renders a native h1–h6, so the document outline comes from the element. The level picks a default size (h1 3xl, h2 2xl, h3 xl, h4 lg, h5 base, h6 sm) that size can override when the visual and the outline differ. Sizes, weights and spacing come from --pada-heading-* tokens.
whenToUse: For every page and section title.
whenNotToUse: For large numbers or decorative text that isn't a heading: use Text or Stat.
do: Pick the level from the outline (one h1 per page, no skipped levels), then adjust size.
Keep headings short and descriptive.
dont: Don't choose a heading level for its size.
accessibility: Native heading elements give screen-reader users a navigable outline.
components.ai: With Pada, use Heading level 1 for the page title "Billing" and Heading level 3 with size "lg" for the "Payment method" card title.

components.name: Icon
components.summary: An SVG icon from Pada's built-in set that takes the text colour.
components.overview: Icon renders one of Pada's 154 built-in SVG icons by name (tick_1, chevron_down, search …), in the surrounding text colour, at a given size, in stroke or fill. You can also pass your own SVG src. Icons are decorative by default.
whenToUse: Next to labels in buttons, menus and navigation; as status indicators with text.
whenNotToUse: As the only content of a button: use IconButton, which requires a label.
For brand marks: use BrandLogo or PadaLogo.
do: Use one icon per meaning across the product.
Size icons with the icon size tokens so they scale with density.
Give meaningful standalone icons a label.
dont: Don't use icons without text for uncommon actions.
accessibility: Decorative icons are aria-hidden; pass a label when the icon carries meaning on its own.
components.ai: With Pada, add a success Icon "tick_1" (size 16, colour var(--pada-color-success-fg)) before the "Saved" status text, and an Icon "alert_1" with label "Warning" for the error rows.

components.name: InfoIcon
components.summary: A small decorative info glyph.
components.overview: InfoIcon is the 12px "i" glyph used next to labels. It is purely decorative and takes the text colour. React draws the same glyph inside KeyValue and InfoTooltip.
whenToUse: Inside your own composite components, next to text that already explains the meaning.
whenNotToUse: As an interactive help trigger: use InfoTooltip, which is a labelled button.
do: Pair it with visible text or a labelled control.
dont: Don't make it the only signal for important information.
accessibility: Decorative SVG; it has no accessible name.
components.ai: With pada-ds-angular, use ds-info-tooltip (not ds-info-icon) next to the "Seats" label so the explanation is reachable from the keyboard.

components.name: InfoTooltip
components.summary: A small info icon that explains the thing next to it.
components.overview: InfoTooltip is a small info icon button next to a label or value that opens a Tooltip on hover and keyboard focus. It is named "More info about {label}".
whenToUse: For short explanations of terms, metrics and settings that most people don't need.
whenNotToUse: For information needed to complete a task: put it in the field description.
For rich content: use Popover.
do: Keep the text to one or two sentences.
Pass label so the button's name says what it explains.
dont: Don't put several info icons in one row.
accessibility: A native button; Escape closes the tooltip; the trigger references the tooltip only while it is open.
components.ai: With Pada, add an InfoTooltip after the "Seats" label with label "Seats" and text "Seats are billed monthly, per active member."

components.name: Kbd
components.summary: A keyboard key or shortcut, as in "Press ⌘ K".
components.overview: Kbd renders keys as small key caps inside a native <kbd>. Pass keys for a combination.
whenToUse: In tooltips, menus, help text and command palettes to teach shortcuts.
whenNotToUse: For code: use CodeSnippet.
do: Show the platform's modifier (⌘ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere).
Use the same key names everywhere ("Esc", "Enter").
dont: Don't use Kbd for non-keyboard input.
accessibility: Native <kbd> elements; symbols like ⌘ are read by screen readers, so pair them with a text alternative where it matters.
components.ai: With Pada, add Kbd hints to the menu items: Save (⌘ S), Undo (⌘ Z), and a "Press ⌘ K to search" hint in the header.

components.name: KeyValue
components.summary: A label on the left and a value on the right.
components.overview: KeyValue pairs a label with a value for settings and detail panels, with an optional info tooltip on the label. The value can be any content.
whenToUse: For a few labelled values in a panel or card.
whenNotToUse: For many fields from data: use DescriptionList.
For editable values: use form fields.
do: Keep labels short and aligned; put units in the value.
Use the info tooltip for terms that need explaining.
dont: Don't use it for long text values.
accessibility: The label and value are read in order; the info tooltip is a labelled button.
components.ai: With Pada, show the plan details as KeyValue rows: Plan (Team), Seats (12 of 20, with an info tooltip), Renews on (date) and Owner (Avatar with name).

components.name: PadaLogo
components.summary: The Pada logo as inline SVG: mark, wordmark or both.
components.overview: PadaLogo draws the Pada mark, the "Pada . design" wordmark, or the lockup of both, as inline SVG. Tones are colour, accent (follows the theme's accent) and mono.
whenToUse: In products built with Pada that credit the system, and on Pada's own pages.
whenNotToUse: For third-party logos: use BrandLogo.
do: Use the mark alone where space is tight (favicons, collapsed sidebars).
Use the mono tone on busy backgrounds.
dont: Don't redraw or stretch the mark.
accessibility: Named by title; mark it decorative when the name is already present in text.
components.ai: With Pada, show the PadaLogo lockup (tone accent) in the sidebar header, switching to the mark variant when the sidebar is collapsed.

components.name: Separator
components.summary: A thin line between content, horizontal or vertical.
components.overview: Separator draws a hairline between groups of content, horizontally or vertically, using the border token.
whenToUse: Between groups in menus, toolbars and long panels.
whenNotToUse: Instead of spacing; most groups only need more space between them.
do: Mark purely visual separators as decorative.
dont: Don't stack separators with borders on cards and sections.
accessibility: role="separator" with aria-orientation, or hidden from assistive technology when decorative.
components.ai: With Pada, put a vertical decorative Separator between the filters and the actions in the toolbar.

components.name: Stat
components.summary: A key figure with a label, delta, description and chart slot.
components.overview: Stat shows a KPI: a label, a big value that counts to its new number when it changes, an optional delta coloured by whether the change is good, a description and a chart slot for a sparkline. Values and deltas are formatted with Intl.NumberFormat options.
whenToUse: On dashboards and summaries for the few numbers that matter.
whenNotToUse: For tables of numbers: use Table.
do: Format values (formatOptions) and deltas (percent) and say what the delta compares to ("vs last month").
Use invertTrend for metrics where down is good (churn, errors).
Keep a row of stats to four or fewer.
dont: Don't show a delta without a comparison period.
accessibility: Screen readers get the final value, never the frames of the count animation; the animation is off under reduced motion.
components.ai: With Pada, show a row of Stats in Cards: Revenue (USD, delta +12.4% vs last month), Active users, and Churn (percent, invertTrend), each with a small sparkline in the chart slot.

components.name: TagGroup
components.summary: A wrapping list of removable tags with one tab stop.
components.overview: TagGroup lists removable tags (active filters, selected recipients) as one keyboard unit. Arrow keys move between the tags' remove buttons, Delete or Backspace removes the focused tag, and focus moves to the next tag once it is gone. Available in Angular; React has it on the roadmap.
whenToUse: To show active filters or selections that people can remove one by one.
whenNotToUse: For typing new values: use TagInput.
For static labels: use Tags.
do: Name the group with label ("Active filters").
Offer a "Clear all" button next to long groups.
dont: Don't mix removable and non-removable tags in one group.
accessibility: role="list" with each tag a listitem; one tab stop with arrow keys and Home/End.
components.ai: With pada-ds-angular, show the active filters in a ds-tag-group label="Active filters" with a removable ds-tag per filter that removes it on (remove).

components.name: Tags
components.summary: A tinted label for categories and metadata.
components.overview: Tags label items with categories and metadata: "Design", "Q3", "Owner: Ada". They come in six variants (neutral, primary, secondary, success, danger, royal) with an optional leading icon. In Angular, ds-tag with removable adds a remove button.
whenToUse: For categories, topics and attributes on cards and rows.
whenNotToUse: For status: use Badge.
For entering values: use TagInput.
do: Keep tag text short and consistent in case.
Use colour to group categories, not to rank them.
dont: Don't use the deprecated hue names (gray, blue …); use the variants.
accessibility: Plain text; a removable tag's button is named "Remove <label>".
components.ai: With Pada, show the article's topics as Tags (variant neutral) under the title, and its status as a Badge.

components.name: Text
components.summary: Text set on the type scale.
components.overview: Text applies the type scale to any element: size, weight, family, line height and colour from tokens. In React choose the element with as; in Angular put dsText on the element you want.
whenToUse: For body copy, captions, labels and helper text that need a specific step on the scale.
whenNotToUse: For headings: use Heading so the outline is correct.
do: Use semantic colour tokens (--pada-color-fg-muted) for secondary text.
Choose the right element (p for paragraphs, span inline).
dont: Don't set raw font sizes; pick a size from the scale so it follows --pada-type-base.
accessibility: Text inherits the element's semantics; muted colours still meet contrast in both themes.
components.ai: With Pada, render the card description as Text size "sm" in var(--pada-color-fg-muted) inside a p element.

components.name: AspectRatio
components.summary: Keeps content at a fixed shape; media inside fill it.
components.overview: AspectRatio keeps its content at a fixed width-to-height ratio (16/9, 4/3, 1). Images and videos inside fill it and are cropped to fit, so layouts don't jump as media loads.
whenToUse: For thumbnails, video embeds, maps and cover images.
whenNotToUse: For text content whose height should grow.
do: Use the media's real ratio where possible to avoid cropping important parts.
Set alt text on the images inside.
dont: Don't nest scrollable content inside.
accessibility: A layout wrapper with no role; accessibility comes from the media inside.
components.ai: With Pada, wrap each project thumbnail in an AspectRatio of 16/9 inside its Card, with the image covering the area and meaningful alt text.

components.name: Container
components.summary: Centres page content at a readable maximum width.
components.overview: Container centres content with a maximum width (sizes from small to full) and side gutters that grow on wider screens.
whenToUse: As the outer wrapper of page content and marketing sections.
whenNotToUse: Inside cards or panels that already constrain width.
do: Use the small size for reading (articles, forms) and larger sizes for dashboards.
Render it as the right element with as (main, section).
dont: Don't nest containers.
accessibility: No role of its own; choose a semantic element with as.
components.ai: With Pada, wrap the settings page in a Container size "md" rendered as main, with a Stack of sections inside.

components.name: Grid
components.summary: CSS grid layout with token gaps, fixed or auto-fitting columns.
components.overview: Grid lays out children in columns with gaps from the space tokens, so spacing follows density. Use fixed columns, or minItemWidth for as many columns as fit.
whenToUse: For card grids, dashboards and galleries.
whenNotToUse: For a single row or column: use Stack.
do: Prefer minItemWidth so the grid adapts to the screen without breakpoints.
Keep items the same height within a row.
dont: Don't use a grid to build tables; use Table.
accessibility: Visual order follows DOM order, so keyboard and reading order stay correct.
components.ai: With Pada, lay out the dashboard Stat cards in a Grid with minItemWidth "240px" and gap 4.

components.name: List
components.summary: A vertical list of items, optionally reorderable.
components.overview: List renders ListItem rows. With draggable, items can be reordered with the mouse or keyboard: focus the handle, press Space to lift, move with the arrows and press Space to drop (Escape cancels). Each step is announced, and onReorder reports the new order.
whenToUse: For simple lists of items, and for ordering things (priorities, playlist, steps).
whenNotToUse: For records with several columns: use Table.
For hierarchies: use Tree.
do: Name reorderable lists with label ("Tasks").
Persist the new order as soon as an item is dropped.
dont: Don't rely on drag only; the keyboard route is built in, keep the handle visible.
accessibility: A list with list items; drag handles are buttons with live announcements for lift, move and drop.
components.ai: With Pada, show the sprint backlog as a draggable List labelled "Backlog" whose order is saved through onReorder.

components.name: Resizable
components.summary: Panels separated by handles that people drag to resize.
components.overview: Resizable splits a region into panels with handles between them: an editor and a preview, a list and a detail view. Panels can have minimum sizes and be collapsible. Compose Resizable.Root, Resizable.Panel and Resizable.Handle.
whenToUse: For tools where people tune the layout to their task.
whenNotToUse: For simple pages; fixed responsive layouts are easier to use.
do: Set sensible minimum sizes so panels never become unusable.
Remember sizes per person.
dont: Don't nest many levels of resizable panels.
accessibility: Handles are focusable separators: arrow keys resize, Home/End jump to the limits, Enter collapses a collapsible panel. Named "Resize" unless you pass a label.
components.ai: With Pada, split the editor into a Resizable group: a file tree panel (min 15%, collapsible), a handle, and the editor panel, saving the sizes to local storage.

components.name: ScrollArea
components.summary: A scrolling region with slim, themed scrollbars and faded edges.
components.overview: ScrollArea adds slim, themed scrollbars and faded edges to an overflowing region while keeping native scrolling (touch, wheel, keyboard, snapping, find-in-page).
whenToUse: For panels and lists with their own scroll inside a fixed layout.
For horizontal rows of items.
whenNotToUse: For the main page scroll.
do: Give it an aria-label when content overflows, since it becomes focusable.
Keep only one scrolling area per direction in a view.
dont: Don't hide scrollbars entirely on content people need to explore.
accessibility: When content overflows, the region becomes focusable so keyboard users can scroll it.
components.ai: With Pada, wrap the notifications list in a ScrollArea with max height 400px and aria-label "Notifications".

components.name: Stack
components.summary: Flex layout with token-based gaps.
components.overview: Stack lays out children in a row or column with a gap from the space scale, so spacing follows the density setting. It sets alignment, justification and wrapping, and can render as any element.
whenToUse: For almost every one-dimensional layout: form fields, button rows, card content.
whenNotToUse: For two-dimensional layouts: use Grid.
do: Use space tokens for gaps instead of margins on children.
Use wrap for rows of chips and buttons that may not fit.
dont: Don't nest many Stacks just to add padding; padding belongs to the container.
accessibility: No role; choose the element with as (for example ul for a list).
components.ai: With Pada, lay out the form fields in a column Stack with gap 4 and the footer buttons in a row Stack justified to the end with gap 2.

components.name: ThemeProvider
components.summary: Sets Pada's theme axes for the page or a subtree.
components.overview: ThemeProvider sets the theme attributes (data-theme, data-accent, data-neutral, data-density, data-radius, data-motion, data-contrast) on the page root or on its own element, and shares them through useTheme(). It can remember the choice in storage. ThemeToggle switches light and dark with a view transition.
whenToUse: At the app root to apply and persist the person's theme.
Around a subtree that should look different (a dark sidebar, a compact table).
whenNotToUse: If you only need static attributes: set them on <html> directly.
do: Default the theme to system and let people override it.
Use a custom accent hue for your brand (accent="custom" with a hue).
dont: Don't override individual colours to brand the product; change the knobs.
accessibility: data-motion="reduced" and data-contrast="more" follow the OS settings by default; offer them as preferences too.
components.ai: With Pada, wrap the app in a ThemeProvider target="root" with defaultTheme "system", accent "custom" with our brand hue 262, density "compact" and a storageKey, and add a ThemeToggle to the header.

components.name: FormLabel
components.summary: The 1.x form label. Use Field.
components.overview: FormLabel is the Pada 1.x label. Since 2.0, use Field (Field.Root, Field.Label, Field.Control, Field.Description, Field.Error), which also wires the control's id, description and error. It keeps working until 3.0.
components.ai: Replace Pada FormLabel with Field: wrap each control in Field.Root, use Field.Label, and move help text and errors into Field.Description and Field.Error.

components.name: Loader
components.summary: The 1.x loader. Use Spinner, ProgressCircle or Skeleton.
components.overview: Loader is the Pada 1.x loading indicator. Since 2.0, use Spinner for inline loading, ProgressCircle when progress is known, or Skeleton for content placeholders. It keeps working until 3.0.
components.ai: Replace Pada Loader usages: use Spinner for inline waits, ProgressCircle where a percentage is available, and Skeleton for initial page loads.

components.name: Logo
components.summary: Renamed to BrandLogo.
components.overview: Logo is the old name of BrandLogo (third-party logos by name). Pada's own logo is PadaLogo. The alias keeps working until 3.0.
components.ai: Rename every Pada Logo import and usage to BrandLogo; the props stay the same.

components.name: Modal
components.summary: The 1.x modal. Use Dialog.
components.overview: Modal is the Pada 1.x modal window. Since 2.0 it wraps Dialog, which adds a trigger, a description, a footer and sizes. It keeps working until 3.0.
components.ai: Replace every Pada Modal in this file with Dialog (Dialog.Root, Dialog.Content, Dialog.Header, Dialog.Title, Dialog.Body, Dialog.Footer), keeping the same open state and close handlers.

components.name: Notification
components.summary: The 1.x notification. Use Toaster and toast().
components.overview: Notification is the Pada 1.x notification. Since 2.0, render one Toaster and call toast() / toast.success() …: toasts are queued, stacked, dismissed by swipe and paused on hover. It keeps working until 3.0.
components.ai: Remove Pada Notification components from this app: add one Toaster at the root and replace each notification with a toast.success / toast.danger call carrying the same title and description.

components.name: SideDrawer
components.summary: The 1.x side panel. Use Drawer.
components.overview: SideDrawer is the Pada 1.x side panel. Since 2.0 it wraps Drawer, which adds a trigger, a title, other edges and padding. It keeps working until 3.0.
components.ai: Replace Pada SideDrawer usages with Drawer.Root and Drawer.Content side="right", adding a Drawer.Header with a Drawer.Title for each.
